code.originalText: Two-week review: ambulatory blood pressure result, echocardiogram, metabolic panel, cardiology consultation the same day, and the diagnosis

text.paragraph: Two-week review: blood pressure, echocardiogram and cardiology consultation. [S]

Ms. Hurston returns two weeks after intake and is seen the same day by Dr. Okafor-Whitfield of cardiology after her echocardiogram this morning. The 24-hour ambulatory recording before her first doses averaged 158/96 mmHg (daytime 163/99, night 149/90), with no fall in pressure at night, which confirms stage 2 hypertension. She started chlorthalidone 12.5 mg and amlodipine 5 mg the next morning; her home readings over the past week average 146/88. The morning headaches have gone. She is still breathless on one flight of stairs and her ankles swell a little by evening. She has had no lightheadedness, cramps or palpitations. The echocardiogram shows a preserved ejection fraction with thick heart walls and stiff filling. She met the community health worker last week: her SNAP application is in, and a SHINE counselor will see her on Thursday about drug coverage. [S]

Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (I11.0). Stage 2 hypertension confirmed by ambulatory monitoring, with concentric left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG and echocardiogram. Home average 146/88 after one week on the two-drug combination: improving, not yet at the target below 130/80. Dr. Okafor-Whitfield agrees with the combination and the diagnosis. [S]
Continue chlorthalidone 12.5 mg and amlodipine 5 mg.
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily for primary prevention, with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks.
Home readings twice daily for the week before each visit.

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, NYHA class II (I50.32). Breathlessness, raised NT-proBNP (480 pg/mL), an enlarged left atrium, an E/e' of 15 and concentric hypertrophy with an ejection fraction of 62% establish HFpEF from hypertensive heart disease. Cardiology found no red flags for amyloidosis, valve disease or ischemia. [S]
Dapagliflozin 10 mg daily, with sick-day rules; supplied through the manufacturer's patient assistance program until drug coverage begins.
Daily weights with a written plan; call for a gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week.
Metabolic panel in two weeks.
Pneumococcal vaccine (PCV20) today.

Low income without drug coverage (Z59.6). Generic medicines in 90-day fills cost her little; dapagliflozin has no low-cost generic on her pharmacy's list. [S]
SHINE counselor this week for Extra Help and the Medicare Savings Program.
